subject: Private VPC blueprint: control/data plane demarcation for Quantaplex
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Justin Park <justin.park@quantaplex.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC blueprint: control/data plane demarcation for Quantaplex

Hi Justin —

Thanks for the sync earlier. Attached is the first-pass blueprint we discussed: a single-page reference diagram plus a matrix that maps control-plane components to the Redwood-managed control VPC and data-plane components to Quantaplex's customer VPC. Key asks below:

- Please confirm Quantaplex's preferred egress posture: do you require all outbound traffic to be NATed through your central egress VPC (preferred), or do you want per-tenant egress via customer-managed NAT?
- Validate the proposed broken-out CIDR ranges in the diagram (Attachment: quantaplex-vpc-blueprint-v1.pdf).
- Any constraints on BGP peering or IPSEC tunnels (vendor appliance vs. cloud native)?

High-level decision we propose: Redwood keeps the control plane and its management plane endpoints in a Redwood-managed VPC (we provide the endpoint and certificate rotation). The inference data-plane nodes will live in Quantaplex's VPC; we will deploy a small set of sidecars that handle KV cache, metrics relay, and local prefix caching. This minimizes token egress and keeps customer data in their network boundary.

I've attached an ops-handoff checklist and a small matrix that lists which services require bi-directional connectivity, which can be outbound-only, and which require port white-listing (controlplane-dataplane-matrix.xlsx).

Can Kimberly and Marissa review the security and operational notes below and flag anything we should call out before the architecture review with Quantaplex's engineering team next week?

Thanks,
Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0191

Attachments: quantaplex-vpc-blueprint-v1.pdf (diagram, 1 page), controlplane-dataplane-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), ops-handoff-checklist.docx

From: Justin Park <justin.park@quantaplex.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Infra Team <infra@quantaplex.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@quantaplex.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 13:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC blueprint: control/data plane demarcation for Quantaplex

Thanks Sean, this looks like a good start. Quick responses inline: 

- Egress posture: we prefer central egress through our Transit VPC so security can apply standard DLP and proxy rules.
- CIDRs: the /24s in the draft collide with an internal subnet; we'll provide the up-to-date allocation.
- Tunnels: we run a Palo Alto VM-Series for IPSEC termination today; open to using cloud-native where feasible but prefer appliance until we validate throughput.

A few clarifying Qs: 
1) How do you plan to handle KV cache invalidation when we scale shards? Will that require cross-VPC traffic?
2) Are metrics/telemetry pushed from the sidecars or pulled by Redwood? We prefer push to our collector endpoint.

I'll share our current CIDR/gateway sheet by EOD. Can we also add a short section in the ops checklist about certificate pinning and rotation windows? Our security team is strict about key rollover windows.

-Justin

--
Justin Park
Head of Infrastructure, Quantaplex Inc.
justin.park@quantaplex.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC blueprint: control/data plane demarcation for Quantaplex

Sean / Marissa —

Thanks for the draft. A few security/ops edits I recommend before we present: 

- Control plane endpoints: add an explicit note that we will require mTLS for management RPCs and short-lived certs (7-14 day rotation) unless Quantaplex requires a different window.
- KV cache: design for eventual cross-VPC invalidation using a Redis-backed pub/sub over TLS (outbound from customer VPC to Redwood metrics endpoint). If Quantaplex blocks outbound, we need to plan a VPN-forwarded pull instead.
- Egress rules: label in the diagram which flows are CDN/OS packages (allowlist) versus telemetry (to Quantaplex collector).
- Network ACLs: call out an initial staging ACL that is permissive for the handoff window and a production ACL template we will apply during cutover.

Also: recommend we include an appendix page in the PDF listing the exact port ranges and IPs used by the control-plane health checks (to help their firewall team).

I'll add those changes to the blueprint and push v1.1 to the Drive.

Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Product Security Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Justin Park <justin.park@quantaplex.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 31 Jul 2025 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC blueprint: control/data plane demarcation for Quantaplex

Justin —

Appreciate the fast feedback. Summary / decisions so far: 

1) Egress: Quantaplex will centralize egress through its Transit VPC. Redwood sidecars will be configured to egress via Quantaplex NAT — we will include instructions in the ops checklist for routing and SNAT expectations.
2) KV cache invalidation: primary plan is outbound push-based invalidation (pub/sub) over TLS to a Redwood-managed endpoint. Fallback: if Quantaplex blocks outbound, we'll switch to a pull model tunneled over the IPSEC appliance.
3) Metrics/telemetry: sidecars will PUSH metrics to the Quantaplex collector endpoint (per your preference). We'll document envelope schema and batching windows.
4) Cert rotation: propose 10-day rotation for service certs (can tighten to 7 on request). We'll add a cert-pinning appendix for your security team.

Next steps / actions: 
- Marissa: update the ops-handoff-checklist.docx with routing/NAT notes and a cutover ACL template.
- Kimberly: publish blueprint v1.1 with port/IP appendix and the cert rotation language.
- Justin: share your current CIDR allocations and any appliance throughput SLAs.
- I'll schedule a 45-min architecture review with Quantaplex infra and your security lead; proposed times: Thu 08/07 10:00-10:45 PT or Fri 08/08 13:00-13:45 PT — please confirm.

If everyone is aligned I'll hold the meeting for Thu 08/07 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Justin Park <justin.park@quantaplex.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Infra Team <infra@quantaplex.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@quantaplex.com>
Date: Thu, 31 Jul 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC blueprint: control/data plane demarcation for Quantaplex

Sean / team —

All good on our side. Confirming: Thu 08/07 10:00-10:45 PT works for me and I'll loop in our security lead, Samantha. We'll send CIDR sheet and current appliance throughput numbers by EOD Friday 08/01.

Two small asks to include prior to the review: 
- Add a short rollback plan in the ops checklist (steps + estimated rollback time).
- Include a clear signal for "ready for cutover" (we use: infra smoke tests green + <1% 5xx over 30m + replicated model artifacts present).

Appreciate the clarity here — looking forward to the review.

Best,
Justin

--
Justin Park
Head of Infrastructure, Quantaplex Inc.
